key_insight: Thermal insulation can relax the need to prevent carrier-to-lattice energy transfer, while absorber ohmic heat can be partially recycled into electrical work at the Carnot efficiency.
engineering_relevance: The analysis identifies absorber thermal insulation and suppression of contact-mediated heat leakage as design targets for high-efficiency solar cells.
method: Thermodynamic analysis of nonideal hot-carrier and hot-absorber solar cells
Inclusion of finite absorber conductivity and ohmic heating
Sensitivity analysis for finite contact-mediated heat leakage
evidence_signal: The abstract reports thermodynamic-limit calculations and heat-leakage sensitivity analysis, not experimental device efficiencies; 85.4% is the cited ideal hot-carrier efficiency limit.
watch_item: High efficiencies assume ideal energy-selective contacts and negligible parasitic contact conductance, so they are not practical device-efficiency projections.
paper_title: Nonideal Absorbers in Hot-Carrier and Hot-Absorber Solar Cells: Losses and Heat Recycling
